objective: Make the Cloud IaC module-registry protocol gate fail closed when release-index S3/GCS object-source rows are not mirrored by protocol download response locations.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: The module registry download endpoint returns a JSON location value that OpenTofu uses as the module source location.
OpenTofu module sources include registry, HTTP archive, S3 bucket, and GCS bucket source patterns, and may use ambient credentials outside the source metadata.
S3 object versions have version IDs; this ChangeSet uses local version-id metadata only and performs no S3 calls.
Cloud Storage objects have generation metadata; this ChangeSet uses local generation metadata only and performs no GCS calls.
Artifact verification requires explicit verification evidence; signing/SLSA/VSA verification remains non-claimed.

red_tests.summary: The protocol gate accepted a release-index row with pinned S3 archive_source_location metadata while the protocol download fixture still returned a local /artifacts/modules path.

verification.summary: Focused protocol tests passed, including pinned S3/GCS object-source fixtures and object-source-to-local download drift rejection.

implemented_claims: The Cloud IaC module-registry protocol gate parses optional release-index archive_source_location, archive_source_integrity_sha256, archive_source_version_id, and archive_source_generation metadata.
Protocol download response locations can now be local /artifacts/modules paths or safe OpenTofu s3::https:// / gcs::https:// object-source values.
Local archive release-index rows continue to require protocol download response location to equal artifact_url_path.
Object-source release-index rows require protocol download response location to exactly mirror archive_source_location.
Object-source release-index rows require object-source fixture source_kind metadata and local integrity/provider pin metadata before protocol fixtures can pass.
Unsafe object-source text, orphan pins, missing provider pins, wrong-provider pins, and mismatched integrity fail closed in the protocol gate.
explicit_non_claims: No live S3 or GCS read/write/list/head/precondition execution.
No object-store bucket provisioning, IAM policy enforcement, signed URL generation, CDN integration, or secret/credential management.
No deployed module registry endpoint, production auth/Cedar policy runtime, tenant identity, persistence, database adapter, TLS termination, measured SLO, DR, or capacity telemetry.
No signing, SLSA, VSA, provider runtime, tofu test/plan/apply, Argo CD/Kubernetes rollout, cloud provisioning, production readiness, or FD-001 tenant workload hosting.
No materialized production object-store release-index row; current live release-index and protocol fixtures remain local archive routes.
false_green_findings_closed: The protocol fixture gate can no longer pass a release-index object-source row whose download response still returns the local artifact path instead of the release-index archive_source_location.
known_gaps: Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required is not claimed green.
Aggregate ./bin/oya gate run-all is not claimed green unless freshly rerun and proven.
Live object-store adapters, request precondition execution, signed module verification, production auth/Cedar, and deployment evidence remain future slices.
Repo-local release-index and protocol fixtures still use local archive routes; no production object-store release index has been materialized.

findings: Kept the slice narrow: protocol fixture coherence only, no fake object-store endpoint or deployment.
Hardens the module distribution control plane by ensuring registry protocol fixtures mirror immutable object-source metadata before live adapters exist.
RED fixture proved local-path drift passed before the fix; GREEN fixtures cover S3 and GCS object-source paths plus drift rejection.
Existing local archive fixtures remain compatible; object-source behavior activates only when archive_source_location is present.
Focused protocol tests, fmt/check/clippy, governance gates, and full scoped Cloud IaC gate suite passed.

alternatives_named: Add object-source protocol coherence gate now
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A local protocol coherence gate is the smallest honest step after release-index pinning and before credentials/buckets/adapters exist.
rejected_reasons: Live adapters need real object storage, IAM, credentials, precondition calls, and deployment evidence outside this slice.
Local-path-only protocol fixtures create a false-green gap once release-index object-source rows appear.

findings: Object-source protocol metadata rejects credential-like text and must stay coherent with integrity/pin metadata before fixture validation can pass.
Parser/gate-only validation adds no live network or object-store I/O path.
Version/generation metadata is explicit and locally gated; compliance-grade retention/precondition evidence remains non-claimed.
Current repo-local /artifacts/modules fixtures remain valid because no live release-index row has archive_source_location.
Bad object-source protocol metadata fails during gate validation before any runtime module-registry serving claim.
ChangeSet is tied to Oya VCS claim, source/tests, manifest/tasks, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain rows.
Used Oya VCS claim; avoided raw git/gh; read root hub and operating contract; kept /plan complementary-only; did not claim production/hyperscaler completion.
No new dependencies were introduced. Strict dependency-seam gate is run as closeout evidence.

review_findings: No critical/high issues found for the local protocol fixture gate scope. Live object-store adapter/precondition verification remains an explicit gap.

Scoped retired-vocabulary used a temporary corpus containing the claimed files because the gate accepts directory corpus roots and broader oya-dev-cli directories contain unrelated pre-existing retired vocabulary drift.
